questions.question: Describe the Moon as Earth's natural satellite, including its distance, gravity and surface features.
questions.expected_answer: A satellite orbits a larger body; the Moon is Earth's only natural satellite. It is a rocky body about a quarter of Earth's diameter, about 384 000 km away, with gravity about one sixth of Earth's. It has no atmosphere and no liquid water, so temperatures are extreme; its surface is covered in dust and craters made by meteorite impacts, dark lava plains (maria) and lighter highlands.

questions.question: Explain why we always see the same side of the Moon and what keeps it in its orbit.
questions.expected_answer: The Moon takes about 27,3 days to orbit the Earth and the same time to rotate once on its axis, so the same side always faces the Earth (tidal locking). Earth's gravity pulls the Moon towards it, while the Moon's sideways motion carries it forward; together these make it travel in a curved orbit around the Earth instead of flying off or falling in.

questions.question: Explain why the Moon shines and what causes its phases, naming the phases in order from new Moon to full Moon.
questions.expected_answer: The Moon does not make its own light; it reflects sunlight. Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun; as the Moon orbits the Earth, we see different amounts of the lit half, causing the phases. Order: new Moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full Moon (then waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent).
